clue.text: E Anglian lakes order a cutter

parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are the lakes and waterways of East Anglia, in eastern England
to give the word is to give an order or command

explanation.surface: Someone in East Anglia orders a boat to cut through the lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cutter' looks like a boat for the Broads, but it is a weapon that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-bladed sword is a weapon for slashing, so it is literally a cutter.

clue.text: Rustic's family deserts him -what a blow!

indicators.note: the family walking out on the rustic means that part of the word for him is taken away

parts.note: a bumpkin is a rustic, an unsophisticated country person
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A country fellow's relatives abandon him, and he exclaims at the blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' points back to the rustic; with KIN gone from BUMPKIN, what is left is the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a knock or jolt, a kind of blow.

clue.text: An operatic hero lost his head in this bacchanal

indicators.note: the hero losing his head means the first letter of his name is dropped

parts.note: Porgy is the hero of Gershwin's opera Porgy and Bess

explanation.surface: An opera hero goes wild at a drunken party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost his head' sounds like losing control at the party, but it removes P from PORGY.
explanation.definitionFit: A bacchanal is a drunken revel, the same as a wild debauched party.

clue.text: In staged rite, characters lose cohesion

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the staged rite are what get rearranged here

explanation.surface: During a staged ritual, the actors fall apart and lose their unity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like the actors in the rite; it tells you to work with the letters of IN STAGED RITE, which rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To disintegrate is to break up into pieces, which is to lose cohesion.

clue.text: Comparatively bad areas Dyfed or Kent, perhaps?

parts.note: Dyfed is a county in Wales, in the west of Britain, so W
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, so SE

explanation.surface: Asking which region is less pleasant, Welsh Dyfed or Kent in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'areas' and 'perhaps' tell you Dyfed and Kent are examples of regions given by compass points: W for west and SE for south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Worse is the comparative form of bad.

clue.text: Reserve one in Reformed Church centre

indicators.note: one goes inside the rest, so its letter is placed within the rearranged letters
reformed means formed again, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from joining a reformed church centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' looks like a kind of church, but it is the anagram signal; the CE abbreviation for the Church of England joins the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a quality of character means reticence, a reluctance to speak openly.

clue.text: Drop it by order

indicators.note: by here means placed next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is told to abandon something by official instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a command but is an honour; 'by' just sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is to drop it.

clue.text: Court in which mother is promised a view, say?

indicators.note: say tells you the phrase is spoken and the letters entered match its sound

parts.note: mother is MA, and promised a view is SHALL SEE, so the phrase is Ma shall see

explanation.surface: A mother assured she will get a good view inside a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Marshalsea was an old English court, and the London prison attached to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marshalsea was a historic English law tribunal run by the royal household, later known for its debtors' prison.

clue.text: Revolutionary movement with highest attainment level is Continental …

parts.note: a trot is a movement or gait of a horse
as in the sky's the limit, the sky is the highest point one can reach
ist is German, a Continental language, for is

explanation.surface: A revolutionary movement reaches great heights across Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 11 down; on its own this clue is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Leon Trotsky is a revolutionary of a particular Marxist kind.

clue.text: He tries to give old priests free treats

parts.note: the Magi were ancient Persian priests

indicators.note: free means loose or released from order, so the letters of the word treats are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man tries to hand out sweets to elderly clergymen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He tries' sounds like effort, but it means one who tries cases in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate hears cases in a lower court, so he tries offenders.

clue.text: Archduke, for one, brings forward end of disturbance

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for disturbance is taken from the back and put at the front

parts.note: a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A nobleman stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archduke' looks like a nobleman, but it is Beethoven's Archduke piano work for three players.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Archduke is a piece for three instruments, a famous example of the genre.

clue.text: … like this person, do we assume, relatively speaking?

definitions.text: … like this person, do we assume, relatively speaking?

parts.words: like this person, do we assume, relatively speaking
parts.note: following on from Continental in 8 down, a relative who is like this person from mainland Europe would be a German one

explanation.surface: Wondering whether someone from the Continent is a relation of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 8 down's 'Continental': a German relative, but in fact a first cousin, child of one's aunt or uncle.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane in old usage meant of the same parents' line, so the phrase names a first cousin.

clue.text: Habit not normally in evidence, supporting duds?

parts.note: something supporting another thing lies under it
duds is slang for garments

explanation.surface: A nun's habit is not usually seen, worn under worn-out things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a nun's robe or a custom; here it is dress worn out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is a form of dress that is normally hidden from view.

clue.text: Many a short contest held by Miss Liddell's partner

indicators.note: held by means the other pieces sit inside the name

parts.note: Alice Liddell was the girl who inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
comp is a shortened form of competition

explanation.surface: Lots of quick games are hosted by Miss Liddell's companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice Liddell was the real girl behind Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland; the short contest and the hundred sit just after her opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is a partner in a crime or scheme.

clue.text: Assignment left in a particular spot

indicators.note: left goes in, so its letter is placed within the rest

parts.note: a location is a particular place or spot

explanation.surface: A task was left at a specific place.
explanation.definitionFit: An allocation is a share given out, an assignment of resources.

clue.text: Student member in a tipsy state after pass

indicators.note: the member and the rest come after the pass in the answer

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
a leg is a limb, or member, of the body

indicators.note: a tipsy state is unsteady, so the letters of in a are jumbled

explanation.surface: A student is drunk after passing an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' sounds like passing an exam but is a mountain pass; 'tipsy state' rearranges IN A to IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A collegian is a member of a college, so a student.

clue.text: Never satisfied, Titania's changed direction

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name of the fairy queen with the s of the possessive
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Titania, queen of the fairies, restlessly alters course.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Titania's gives its S to the anagram; E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiate is an old form meaning insatiable, unable to be filled or contented.

clue.text: Excursion for everyone within the bounds of Surrey

indicators.note: everyone sits within, so its letters are placed inside the outside pair
the bounds of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A day trip for the whole group in the Surrey countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden sortie or a short trip out.

clue.text: Reputation of circle displaying 19

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
19 across is severity; dour means severe and stern

explanation.surface: The standing of a club that shows severity.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' sends you to 19 across, a word for severity; take an adjective from it, DOUR. 'Reputation' is the sense in 'in good odour'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in good or bad odour is to have good or bad standing, so the word can mean repute.

clue.text: Severity new in a novelist's son

indicators.note: new goes in, so its letter is placed within the rest

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy, so Sterne's

explanation.surface: A novelist's son shows a fresh harshness.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside STERNE'S S, after STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternness is harshness or strictness, the quality of being severe.

clue.text: One generally introduced to get rid of ill feeling?

definitions.text: One generally introduced to get rid of ill feeling?

parts.words: One generally introduced to get rid of ill feeling
parts.note: a doctor whose title is preceded by the word general, there to cure people who feel ill

explanation.surface: A peacemaker brought in to end resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill feeling' looks like resentment, but it is literally sickness; 'generally introduced' means the title is preceded by 'general', a family doctor in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A general practitioner is a family doctor who treats patients who feel unwell.

clue.text: Happen to recognize officer with dog

parts.note: OC stands for officer commanding
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone may chance to spot an officer walking his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recognize' is a loose link here: the phrase 'occur to' means to come to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To occur is to take place or come about.

clue.text: Read quickly through second Kipling novel

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel of India

explanation.surface: Someone races through a second Kipling book.
explanation.definitionFit: To skim a text is to glance over it fast without close attention.

clue.text: King Edward thus erected his statue in London

parts.note: ER stands for Edwardus Rex, Latin for King Edward

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: King Edward put up a statue of himself in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' points to the answer, not to the king: the statue in Piccadilly Circus, London, is commonly called by the love god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged figure in Piccadilly Circus is popularly known as the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Bird one's following in the same passage

indicators.note: one's comes after the other piece in the answer

parts.note: ib is short for ibidem, Latin for in the same place, used in references
one's is I'S, one is I and 's is is

explanation.surface: A bird seen again in the same stretch of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' sounds like a migration but refers to a text citation.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: He provides for strikers and seeks to form a union

explanation.surface: A union organiser supports strikers and seeks to build a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikers' and 'union' suggest a trade union, but the strikers are things struck to light and the union is marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes the little sticks used for lighting fires provides for strikers; one who sets couples up hopes to see them wed.

clue.text: Producer of lava .and, in France, sodium

parts.note: et is French for and
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: A producer of lava and, in France, of sodium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is famous for spewing out molten rock.

clue.text: Underground dwarfs heard marking time?

indicators.note: heard means the words are spoken, and the answer matches their sound

parts.note: the Metro is an underground railway, and gnomes are dwarfs

explanation.surface: Dwarfs underground could be heard keeping time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marking time?' is the definition: devices that mark the beat for musicians. The silent G of the gnomes vanishes when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that tick at a set tempo keep the beat for musicians, so they literally mark time.
